C0.quote: A committee of N (odd) voters must approve or reject each of K
C0.note: Vote trading among voters before majority voting on binary proposals; treated as a procedure with strategic aspects.

C1.quote: We explore this subject with a laboratory experiment.
C1.note: Main results are lab data. Stability and convergence theory is a secondary part (EQ). Random-trading simulations are a benchmark (SI).

C2.1.quote: We call v = (v1 ; :::; vN ) a vote allocation

C2.2.quote: each voter's dominant strategy is to cast all votes in his possession
C2.2.note: Voters cast (possibly multiple) votes for or against each binary proposal. None of the listed formats fits.

C2.3.quote: represented by a proﬁle of values, Z

C2.4.quote: dominant strategy is to cast all votes in his possession
C2.4.note: Final votes are stated to equal sincere preferences, with the dominant strategy as the reason. Experiment footnote 13 repeats this.

C3.1.quote: voting in the preferred direction is a dominant strategy
C3.1.note: Strategy is in trading only. Voting is sincere (automatic in the lab).

C3.2.quote: dominant strategy is to cast all votes in his possession

C3.3.quote: voting in the preferred direction is a dominant strategy
C3.3.note: Binary proposals, so sincere voting is dominant.

C4.1.note: The input format is not RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH or PAIR.

C5.1.note: Results concern stability, vote holdings, outcomes and trade types. Payoff gains test trader behaviour and do not evaluate rules by welfare. Efficiency appears only in the introduction.

VOT.quote_behav: sequences of trades yielding myopic strict gains to both traders
VOT.quote_info: conveys to all voters complete information
VOT.note: Voters trade to gain payoffs, myopically in the model. Voting itself is sincere or automatic.

ORG.note: The experimenter and computer only run the protocol.

C7.1.note: Only the voter type is present.

C8.1.quote: Elementary Pivot Algorithm is any mechanism generating a sequence of trades
C8.1.note: The pivot algorithm is a myopic best-response-like dynamic. Stability is a pairwise, coalition-style concept, and farsighted stability uses the farsighted core. Voting uses a dominant strategy.

C8.2.quote: The theory is based on the concept of a stable vote allocation

C9.1.note: The abstract, introduction and conclusion describe lab findings and future research. They make no claims on institutions, voter welfare or which rule to use.
